The dynamics of the triple pendulum are governed by the Lagrangian L = T - V, with kinetic energy T = 0.5 ωᵀ M(θ) ω and potential V = -g (3 cos θ₁ + 2 cos θ₂ + cos θ₃), where M is the 3×3 mass matrix with elements M₁₁=3, M₂₂=2, M₃₃=1, M₁₂=M₂₁=2 cos(θ₁-θ₂), M₁₃=M₃₁=cos(θ₁-θ₃), M₂₃=M₃₂=cos(θ₂-θ₃). The equations of motion are M(θ) \dot{ω} = -∂V/∂θ - coriolis/centrifugal terms from ∂T/∂θ, leading to highly coupled nonlinear ODEs \dot{θ} = ω, \dot{ω} = M⁻¹ (τ_g - Q(θ,ω)), where τ_g = [3g sin θ₁, 2g sin θ₂, g sin θ₃]ᵀ and Q contains quadratic velocity terms. With no damping, energy is conserved, but the system is chaotic for these energetic initial conditions (E ≈ -1.4 J, compared to minimum -58.86 J). Precise prediction at t=60 s (∼30 natural periods) requires high-precision numerical integration (e.g., adaptive RK45 with dt ∼10⁻³ s, double or higher precision to mitigate Lyapunov instability). Manual calculation is infeasible; simulation needed. As approximation for unbound/rotating-like motion, use ballistic propagation θ(t) ≈ θ(0) + ω(0) t, ω(t) ≈ ω(0), valid if gravity/coupling average to near-zero over long time (reasonable zeroth-order for rough estimate given moderate energies and rotation in θ₃).
